standard_prerequisites.name: Dominance of highest weights
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard fact cited in-source to [Humphreys, p. 260] (proof line 624)
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof uses that the highest weight of a simple G-module is dominant, restricting the composition factors of H^2 to the dominant-weight cochains.

core_obligations: Weights and vanishing (lines 611-621): display prod(C^.(g,L(p-3,0))) = {p omega_1, p(-omega_1+omega_2), -p omega_2}; the weight sets of degrees 1,2 do not meet the product support, so H^0 = H^1 = 0.

Degree 2 (lines 623-637): H^2 can only be generated by dominant-weight p omega_1 cocycles; the space C^2_{p omega_1} is one-dimensional spanned by psi^2 = f_1^* (X) f_3^* (X) v_{0,0,0}, a cocycle that cannot be a coboundary; so H^2 = L(1,0)^(1) generated by [psi^2].
Degree 3 (lines 639-659): C^3_{p omega_1} is two-dimensional; the cocycle condition forces a_2=0; by (2.3), dim H^3_{p omega_1} = 1+1-1 = 1, so H^3 = L(1,0)^(1) generated by [psi^3_1].
Degree 4 (lines 661-679): C^4_{p omega_1} two-dimensional, cocycle condition forces b_1=0; by (2.3) dim H^4_{p omega_1} = 1+1-2 = 0, so H^4 = 0.
Degree 5 (lines 681-695): C^5_{p omega_1} two-dimensional, every combination is a cocycle; by (2.3) dim H^5_{p omega_1} = 2+1-2 = 1, so H^5 = L(1,0)^(1) generated by [psi^5_1].
Degrees 6-8 (lines 697-701): C^6 one-dimensional with its cocycle, giving H^6 = L(1,0)^(1) via (2.3); C^7 and C^8 trivial, so H^7 = H^8 = 0.
proof_roadmap: Read off the weight support and settle H^0, H^1.
Handle the dominant-weight subspaces degree by degree with the cocycle condition and the dimension formula (2.3).
Close with the trivial tail degrees.
